headline: This law says federal transportation officials can require sleep-disorder screening or treatment for commercial truck and bus drivers only through a formal rulemaking process.
what_it_does: The law limits how the Department of Transportation can impose sleep-apnea or other sleep-disorder screening, testing, or treatment on people who drive commercial motor vehicles. Any such new or revised requirement must go through a formal rulemaking proceeding before the department can enforce it. The law applies only to requirements adopted on or after September 1, 2013.

who_it_affects.how: They could be subject to a sleep-disorder screening or treatment requirement only if the Department of Transportation adopts it through a formal rulemaking process.
The Department of Transportation must use a formal rulemaking proceeding before it can implement or enforce these sleep-disorder requirements.
Any new federal sleep-disorder screening or treatment rule for their drivers would follow the formal rulemaking process first.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted October 15, 2013; it applies to sleep-disorder requirements adopted on or after September 1, 2013.
